title: Finite-dimensional first-order interpretations
summary: Represent each interpreted object by a finite coordinate block, translate nested function terms, and transfer native first-order truth and consequences.
abstract: An ordered pair can represent one object even when neither coordinate alone can do so. Finite-dimensional interpretations make this idea precise by selecting a definable set of tuples inside an existing structure and defining operations and relations on those tuples. Each quantified variable becomes a fresh block of coordinates, and function graphs determine whole output tuples. We prove that the resulting first-order translation preserves truth on the selected domain and transfers theories and their consequences. A two-coordinate example shows how nested functions are translated, while the one-coordinate case recovers the earlier interpretation construction.
